ella: hey all — first week! quick Q: I created a key in Console but when I try streaming completions I sometimes get a 429 with "rate_limit_exceeded". is the hosted key the same quota as sandbox keys?
opsbot: welcome, ella :tada: Quick facts: sandbox keys = dev/test quotas; hosted (paid) keys follow your org's quota and rate limits. See Console -> API Keys for which key type. If you hit 429 the response includes `Retry-After` header.
ella: oh nice, thanks. is there a concrete difference for streaming? like token rate vs request rate?
mike: short answer: yes. Sandbox enforces lower per-minute requests and lower concurrent streams. Hosted limits are org-level and token-aware. Streaming typically counts both initial request and per-token pacing under our rate engine.
ella: got it. any recommended retry/backoff pattern we use?
tanvi: we recommend exponential backoff with jitter. simple pattern: 500ms * 2^n + jitter, cap at ~5s. also respect `Retry-After`. for streaming, try smaller `max_tokens` or lower `temperature` during retries.
ella: is there a way to check my current quota as a new hire? I don’t see usage metrics in Console yet.
mike: you won't see org-level metrics until your account is mapped. run the internal CLI to check quotas quickly: `rictl users quotas show --user ella` (ask infra to map your github email if this errors).
ella: ran that, got permission denied. who should I ping?
opsbot: infra request: please file an access ticket at https://redwood.internal/it-requests with subject "map user to org for quota view" and tag @infra.
ella: done. thanks. one more: I hit a 429 while testing embeddings with batch size 16 — was that because batch size?
alex: embeddings are mostly token-agnostic but batch size affects concurrency. sandbox has low concurrency caps so big batches can trip the request-rate side. for embeddings, we recommend batching to amortize overhead but keep per-request size under 512 vectors for sandbox.
ella: solid. if I need more sandbox quota for a spike during onboarding (a demo), what's the process?
tanvi: file a quick sandbox increase via the onboarding form (linked in #new-hires pinned). for hosted increases you need a billing/usage request to growth — we also accept Slack ping with a short justification. expect 24–48h for hosted quota increases.
ella: perfect. thanks everyone! saved these notes.
mike: one extra tip: to avoid rate surprises, set a fallback model in your client config so the request automatically goes to a lower-cost compatible variant when you get capacity errors. e.g., fallback to `rwkv-small` or a quantized variant.
ella: good idea, will do. :thumbsup:
opsbot: closing checklist: create ticket, attach demo dates, request mapping. good luck! :rocket:
